answer: Random liveness pings can limit sybils. Each epoch, a public seed picks a few unpredictable moments, like a tide arriving at a different hour each day, and every identity must return a signed reply within seconds. One operator running a whole meadow of fake identities needs matching parallel compute and attention at every ping, and each missed reply cuts that identity's rewards. A bridge between epochs carries only identities that kept replying, so attacker cost grows linearly with each fake.
